title: Rise of liberalism
summary: John Locke's Two Treatises of Government, published in 1689, defended the claim that people are by nature free and equal, with rights to life, liberty and property. Because governments exist by the consent of the people, those that fail to protect their rights can be resisted and replaced. The Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy treats Locke as a paradigmatic liberal, for whom only limited government can be justified.

uncertainty.note: Two Treatises of Government was licensed and printed in late 1689 bearing the title page imprint of 1690.

as_recorded.value: Paradigmatic liberals such as Locke maintain that justified limitations on liberty are fairly modest. Only a limited government can be justified
An Essay Concerning Human Understanding (1689, published the same year as the Two Treatise )
Two Treatises of Government , he defended the claim that men are by nature free and equal against claims that God had made all people naturally subject to a monarch

when.display: 1689 (Two Treatises published); liberalism developed long after

importance.justification: Ideas of natural rights and government by consent became central to modern politics.

related.because: Lockean natural rights and consent of the governed formed the direct ideological justification for the American Declaration of Independence.
Liberal doctrines of natural rights and legislative sovereignty shaped the French Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen.

reviewer_note: This outline covers Locke, not all of liberalism, whose later forms differ. Modern research dates the writing of the Treatises to 1679-81. The pin at London is a stand-in.
